report:
**Conclusion: Supported.** Exemestane reduces the *incidence* of breast cancer in postmenopausal women at elevated risk, based principally on the randomized, placebo-controlled MAP.3 trial. Over a median three-year follow-up, invasive breast-cancer incidence was 0.19% per year with exemestane versus 0.55% with placebo—a 65% relative reduction (hazard ratio about 0.35). NCI’s prevention summary reports the same 65% reduction.

This does not establish a reduction in breast-cancer mortality: the trial follow-up was relatively short and had few events. The benefit must also be weighed against aromatase-inhibitor adverse effects (notably musculoskeletal symptoms and bone effects). Guidelines treat exemestane as an option for appropriately selected postmenopausal women at increased risk, rather than a universal preventive medication.

Sources:  
- https://www.nejm.org/doi/full/10.1056/NEJMoa1103507  
- https://www.cancer.gov/types/breast/hp/breast-prevention-pdq  
- https://ascopubs.org/doi/10.1200/JCO.19.01472  
- https://www.uspreventiveservicestaskforce.org/uspstf/recommendation/breast-cancer-medications-for-risk-reduction
